# MarketForge PR & Earned Media

Apply V3 §3.13.

## Global quality rules

- HARO was acquired by Cision, rebranded Connectively, and shuttered late 2024. Don't reference HARO.
- Replacements: Qwoted (most active), Help a B2B Writer (Superpath), Featured.com, SourceBottle, Source of Sources.
- PR works when: original data, founder POV with hook, tied to news cycle.
- AI-automatable for pitch drafting.

## Purpose

1. PR strategy (which media targets, what angles).
2. Reactive PR (responding to journalist queries via Qwoted etc.).
3. Proactive PR (pitching news stories with original data).
4. Press release strategy (when justified).
5. Media list building.
6. Crisis PR planning (basic).

## Inputs
- `channel-strategy.md`, `narrative-and-story.md` (POV + arcs), `competitive-intel.md`, `content-strategy.md` (original research).

## Outputs
- `docs/marketing-plan/07-organic-social/pr-earned-media.md`
- DEC-460 to DEC-465

## Structure

```markdown
# PR & Earned Media

## Strategy summary
- Reactive (Qwoted etc.): cheap, time-of-founder; expect 1-3 placements/month.
- Proactive (data-driven pitches): higher leverage when paired with original research; 1-3 placements per quarterly research project.
- Press releases: rarely useful for SMB (only product launches, funding, major hires).

## Reactive PR (Qwoted etc.)

### Daily routine
- Founder spends 15 min/day scanning queries.
- Reply to 2-3 relevant queries with substantive quote.
- Track placements.

### Tools
- Qwoted (free + paid tiers; most active).
- Help a B2B Writer (Superpath).
- Featured.com (paid).
- SourceBottle (Australia + global).
- Source of Sources.

### Pitch format
- Direct, specific, quotable.
- 50-150 words.
- Specific number / contrarian POV.
- Provides journalist immediately usable copy.

## Proactive PR (data-led)

### When to pitch
- Quarterly original research published.
- Major news cycle moment in category.
- Annual category report.

### Pitch
- 100-200 words.
- 3 lines: lead with data point + relevance to news cycle + offer interview.
- Personalized to journalist (read 3 of their recent pieces; reference).

### Target tier
- Tier 1: WSJ, Bloomberg, Forbes, TechCrunch — rare; needs warm-intro + perfect timing + perfect angle.
- Tier 2: industry publications (Information, Stratechery for tech; Modern Retail for DTC; Marketing Brew etc.).
- Tier 3: newsletters (Lenny's Newsletter, ProductLed, Industry-specific Substack).
- Tier 4: podcast guesting (overlaps with `marketforge-podcast-strategy`).

## Media list

For each target publication / outlet:
- Publication name.
- 2-3 named journalists who cover relevant beat.
- Their recent articles.
- Their pitch preferences (Twitter bio, About page).
- Last contact date.

## Press releases

When justified:
- Funding announcement ($5M+ rounds).
- Major product launch with newsworthy angle.
- Major executive hire.
- Acquisition (incoming or outgoing).

When NOT justified:
- Feature release.
- "We hit X customers."
- "New office opening" (unless strategic).
- Generic "industry insight."

## Crisis PR (basic)

- Designated spokesperson per topic.
- Communication template ready (security incident, outage, major bug).
- "What we say / What we don't say" trained.
- Legal review required before publication.

## Anti-patterns

- Generic "We help [audience] do [thing]" pitches.
- Long pitches (over 300 words).
- Pitching journalists who don't cover the beat.
- Multiple pitches to same journalist same week.
- "Newsworthy" press releases that aren't (most isn't).

## Decision cards
[DEC-460 to DEC-465]

## Kill criteria
- 6-12 months; no tier-1 placements + no brand-search lift + no dark-social mentions → re-evaluate angles + targeting.

## What we are intentionally NOT doing
- Buying placements (paid syndication ≠ earned media).
- Spam-pitching journalists.
- Misrepresenting data for headlines.
- Pitching against trademarks (legal exposure).

## Sources and basis
V3 §3.13.
Connectively / HARO shutdown — practitioner data.
```
